body.statement: Uniformly over \((P_N,\mathcal S_N)\in\mathcal M\), \(\sqrt N\{m_N-\beta\mathbf 1-B_Nq_N(p)\}\) is approximated by \(N_3(0,\gamma H_N)\) in bounded-Lipschitz distance, \(0<c\le\lambda_{\min}(H_N)\le\lambda_{\max}(H_N)\le C<\infty\), and \(\widehat\gamma_N/\gamma\to1\) in probability. The approximation is uniform for signed \(A_N\), including \(A_N=0\), local \(\sqrt N B_N\), diverging \(|\sqrt N B_N|\), and \(p_N\) approaching either fixed endpoint. The proof bounds the exact finite covariance matrices and explicitly makes the boundary, sampling alias, denominator-linearization, and Mat\'ern Bessel remainders \(o(N^{-1/2})\).
body.justification: The uniform actual-design experiment is the statistical kernel absent from the existing identification and fixed-domain covariance literature.
body.gap: Lim and Stein prove filtered lattice cross-periodogram normality, and Keshavarz et al. prove scalar irregular-lattice quadratic-form normality; neither result covers these ratio moments, arbitrary quasi-uniform geometry, or weak disappearance of \(p\).
body.consumer: It converts Guan et al.'s local-scale identifying idea into feasible frequentist inference without nugget variation.
